baseline_models.focus_anchor: The parallel conditionals, the possessive in عبادك, and the closing العزيز الحكيم.
baseline_models.mechanism: Punishment and forgiveness are presented as two live exercises of one jurisdiction. Their status as owned servants keeps them within the divine claim, while invincible power excludes external compulsion and wise judgment makes either outcome an adjudication rather than chance.

activation_trace.role: Inflicted pain and penalty supply the punitive pole of the first conditional.
Owned-servant status keeps the people under one master's claim whichever outcome occurs.
Covering an offense and shielding its bearer from its consequence supply the alternate outcome.
Strength and inviolability make the decision answerable to no pressure outside the decision-maker.
Judgment between parties gives the two conditionals a forensic rather than arbitrary frame.

changed_reading.before: The verse merely lists punishment and forgiveness as opposite possibilities.
changed_reading.after: The verse locates both possibilities inside exclusive, unconstrained, and judicially wise divine jurisdiction.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The first consequence says not that they are guilty but that they are عبادك; the forgiveness consequence turns to second-person praise.
baseline_models.mechanism: The rationale after punishment reasserts belonging rather than supplying an accusation. That can authorize the owner's judgment, but it also refuses to cast the people outside the relationship; the praise of power and wisdom after forgiveness then permits a plea for mercy without making a demand.

activation_trace.role: Ownership makes belonging, not a recital of guilt, the stated fact under punishment.
Humble worship keeps the relational sense of servanthood audible beside legal ownership.
Protection from an offense's effect gives the relational appeal a concrete merciful outcome.
Unassailable strength lets forgiveness be praised without implying that it is owed.
Knowledge that reaches the right judgment entrusts the unspoken plea to a wiser knower.

changed_reading.before: The two clauses are emotionally neutral submission to either result.
changed_reading.after: Submission remains complete, yet the asymmetrical rationales allow belonging itself to carry a restrained plea toward forgiveness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The branch ranges of تعذب, تغفر, العزيز, and الحكيم.
baseline_models.mechanism: Beyond a terminal penalty-versus-acquittal opposition, the branches permit two corrective modes: painful restraint or deprivation, and protective covering. Prevention directed toward repair and strengthening can hold both modes within governance of servants.

activation_trace.role: Withholding, preventing, and weaning recast the punitive verb as severe restraint.
A cover that protects what it encloses makes forgiveness an active shelter rather than simple deletion.
Restraint that blocks corruption for the sake of repair supplies a corrective direction.
Strengthening allows protective mercy itself to function as restoration.

changed_reading.before: Punishment destroys or hurts, whereas forgiveness simply cancels.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, both clauses can describe active governance: one restrains painfully and the other covers protectively, with repair as the inferred direction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier hunting case places deliberate breach inside equivalent compensation, equitable adjudication, pardon for what has passed, and punishment upon return; there العزيز closes a threat of vengeance. When العزيز الحكيم instead closes the forgiveness clause in 5:118, pardon becomes a fully powerful, calibrated judicial act rather than the relaxation of justice.

activation_trace.role: Answering an act with its due consequence supplies the case's proportional architecture.
Actual adjudication in the earlier case concretizes the judicial range later carried by الحكيم.
Equivalence links just assessors and an equivalent substitute, making consequence measured rather than indiscriminate.
Leaving punishment and effacing the past establishes amnesty inside the same legal sequence.
Penalty following recognized wrong supplies the recidivism pole opposite the earlier pardon.
Overmastering power there seals vengeance, making its later placement after forgiveness a meaningful reversal.
Protection from the offense's consequence receives the title previously heard beside retribution.
Right-knowing wisdom governs when measured consequence or pardon fits.

structural_cues: 5:95 moves from deliberate breach through assessed equivalents to pardon for the past and vengeance upon recurrence.
5:98 again places severe punishment and forgiving mercy in one compact declaration.
5:118 attaches العزيز الحكيم specifically to the forgiveness conditional.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a worked proportional case and the shifted placement of العزيز; I infer that this legal calibration informs the focus conditionals. A live alternative is that 5:95 is only a local hunting rule and the shared titles carry no procedural transfer.

changed_reading.before: Punishment and pardon look like an unrestricted binary choice.
changed_reading.after: They remain sovereign alternatives, but the pericope makes them case-sensitive responses in which measured pardon can manifest the same power as retribution.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence says that God knows what is made public and what is concealed, warns that some disclosure would cause harm, then names pardon, forgiveness, and forbearance. This activates the covering branch of تغفر: forgiveness may protect a servant by declining to expose a damaging matter, not only by canceling a sentence after exposure.

activation_trace.role: Emergence into visibility establishes one side of the disclosure boundary known by God.
Concealment and covering establish the hidden side without placing it outside divine knowledge.
Repeated manifestation turns disclosure itself into the operation that may produce harm.
What causes distress supplies the consequence that merciful non-exposure can avert.
Leaving punishment and effacing fault joins withheld disclosure to explicit pardon.
Protective covering immediately names the divine stance after the disclosure warning.
The focus verb inherits the possibility of sheltering what full knowledge need not publicly expose.

structural_cues: 5:99 juxtaposes complete divine knowledge with human disclosure and concealment.
5:101 repeats disclosure, names its possible harm, and closes with pardon, forgiveness, and forbearance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies knowledge, concealment, harmful disclosure, and pardon in sequence; I infer a protective non-exposure arrow between them. Alternatively, the disclosure warning and the forgiveness formula may be adjacent assurances without describing one mechanism.

changed_reading.before: To forgive means only to waive punishment after fault has been fully exposed.
changed_reading.after: Forgiveness can also be protective covering: full knowledge need not become damaging exposure in order for wise judgment to be real.

context_deltas.mechanism: After a detailed witness procedure, the messengers are questioned and Jesus sharply limits his testimony to what he said, knew, and observed while present. Once he was taken, continuous watching belonged to God. The focus conditionals therefore function as a jurisdictional handoff: the bounded witness neither sentences nor acquits but submits the people to the all-knowing judge.

activation_trace.role: Evidence stated from knowledge establishes the pericope's formal testimonial frame.
The asymmetry of what is disclosed to each knower sets a hard boundary around the witness's competence.
Presence with observation distinguishes Jesus's time-limited witness from God's unrestricted witnessing.
Taking the person marks the temporal endpoint after which his direct observation no longer governs.
Continuous guarding and watching transfer complete post-departure oversight to God.
Judicial authority receives the case after the witness has defined the limits of his evidence.

structural_cues: 5:106-108 regulates testimony, challenges compromised evidence, and seeks testimony on its proper face.
5:109 opens the gathering of messengers with a question about how they were answered.
5:116-117 repeatedly contrasts divine knowledge and witnessing with Jesus's limited speech, knowledge, presence, and tenure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a witness protocol and an explicit transfer from limited presence to divine watching; I infer that 5:118 completes a witness-to-judge handoff. Alternatively, the legal procedure may only echo the scene loosely, with the conditionals functioning as devotional deference rather than courtroom form.

changed_reading.before: The speaker personally weighs whether the people deserve punishment or pardon.
changed_reading.after: The speaker refuses the sentencing role after giving bounded testimony and returns the entire case to the only witness and judge with complete reach.

context_deltas.mechanism: The table request seeks food, settled hearts, verified truth, and witness status; it is granted as a manifest sign, after which concealing the truth brings an unmatched punishment. This local sequence makes تعذبهم answer heightened receipt and knowledge rather than bare group identity, while 5:118 strikingly leaves forgiveness live even after that warning.

activation_trace.role: The food-bearing table supplies the concrete gift around which knowledge and responsibility intensify.
Settled assurance identifies the requested gift as an answer to epistemic unease.
Verified truth makes later rejection a response to recognized testimony rather than ignorance alone.
A manifest sign turns the provision into public evidence.
Covering or blocking recognized truth supplies the breach following receipt of the sign.
The explicit after-before relation makes sequence and prior receipt part of culpability.
Three concentrated punishment forms state the exceptional consequence attached to post-sign denial.
The focus verb recalls that severe warning but returns its execution to divine discretion.

structural_cues: 5:112-114 progresses from requested food through reassurance and verification to a manifest sign and provision.
5:113 also makes the recipients prospective witnesses.
5:115 repeats the punishment root three times and explicitly locates denial after the gift.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies gift, reassurance, verified truth, witness status, sign, and post-receipt punishment; I infer that increased receipt intensifies accountability in 5:118. Alternatively, the unmatched threat may concern only that particular sign request and need not characterize all people denoted by them.

changed_reading.before: The possible punishment responds to an unspecified collective fault.
changed_reading.after: The nearby sequence makes punishment answerable to received provision and knowingly covered evidence, yet the final witness still does not foreclose forgiveness.

context_deltas.mechanism: Jesus reports the commanded act, worship God, my Lord and your Lord, and the next verse names the same people Your servants. The movement from verbal obedience to a possessed noun distinguishes performance from status: obedience may fail, but failure does not emancipate anyone from divine ownership or remove them from the Lord's formative claim.

activation_trace.role: Commanded worship supplies the behavioral vocation that the people may or may not enact.
Shared lordship and ownership identify the one authority to whom speaker and hearers belong.
The possessed noun preserves owned status even under the possibility of punishment.
The worship sense keeps their failed or fulfilled vocation audible inside their continuing status.

structural_cues: The imperative from the same root in 5:117 is immediately followed by the possessed plural noun in 5:118.
The pronouns keep the same human group in view across command, witness report, and conditional judgment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the verbal command and the adjacent status noun; I infer a distinction between enacted obedience and inescapable belonging. Alternatively, both forms may carry only the ordinary devotional sense, with no deliberate status-performance contrast.

changed_reading.before: Your servants labels an obedient religious class or merely licenses ownership-based punishment.
changed_reading.after: It can name an inalienable divine claim that persists through disobedience, making belonging relevant to both judgment and mercy.

context_deltas.mechanism: Jesus first refuses speech to which he has no right, then limits his witness, and 5:119 immediately declares that truthfulness benefits the truthful. The focus conditionals can therefore be read as truthfulness enacted through restraint: he says exactly what his knowledge and role permit and does not manufacture either an acquittal or an accusation.

activation_trace.role: Truth that matches reality marks the boundary beyond which the speaker refuses to claim speech.
Benefit rather than harm identifies the eschatological efficacy assigned to truthful speech.
Truth in utterance names the quality that the preceding carefully bounded testimony performs.
Right-knowing wisdom is honored by refusing to speak beyond the witness's competence.

structural_cues: 5:116 ties permissible speech to right and knowledge.
5:117 restricts witness to the duration of presence.
5:119 follows the focus utterance with هذا and a verdict about the benefit of truthfulness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies disciplined speech followed immediately by the benefit of truthfulness; I infer that the focus utterance exemplifies that truthfulness. Alternatively, هذا may designate the whole judgment day rather than point especially to the preceding speech.

changed_reading.before: The conditional wording is evasive or emotionally ambivalent.
changed_reading.after: Its refusal to overstate the case is itself truthful testimony: exact speech leaves sentencing to exact knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing verse expands Your servants into dominion over the heavens, earth, and all within them, then asserts complete capability. This confirms that neither punishment nor forgiveness is forced by inability; العزيز supplies effective power, while الحكيم names the intelligent governance by which unlimited capability takes a fitting form.

activation_trace.role: Universal sovereignty scales the possessive in Your servants from one group to the whole created domain.
Effective capacity rules out inability as the reason for either possible outcome.
Local servant ownership becomes one instance of the universal dominion stated next.
Invincible strength ensures that mercy is not a concession to resistance.
Knowledge that reaches the right result governs how unrestricted power is exercised.

structural_cues: 5:120 immediately closes the pericope by moving from the people as Your servants to universal dominion.
The final assertion of capability follows the focus pairing of might and wisdom.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate universal dominion and capability; I infer that the two focus names distinguish ability from the wisdom governing its exercise. Alternatively, 5:120 may be a general doxological close without specifying how the prior conditionals are decided.

changed_reading.before: The final names are generic praise appended to a plea.
changed_reading.after: They articulate a decision structure: nothing constrains the power to punish or forgive, and wise governance determines its fitting exercise.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the sweetness and abstention branches of ع ذ ب rather than replacing the direct punishment sense. It remains anchored in تعذب and is materially triggered by the nearby eating, table, and provision sequence. Downstream prose should present it only as a cross-domain echo of deprivation after received sustenance, never as the verb's primary lexical meaning.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The root of تعذب carries distant branches of palatable sweetness and abstention from food or drink.

activation_trace.role: Palatable sweetness supplies the positive material whose withdrawal can be felt as loss.
Abstention from eating and drinking converts that loss into a deprivation image.
Literal consumption makes sustenance the recipients' stated desire.
The food-bearing table gives the deprivation image a concrete supplied object.
Nourishing provision frames the sign as sustaining gift, not evidence alone.
The direct penalty branch keeps the material echo subordinate to the explicit punishment sense.

changed_reading.before: Punishment is an undifferentiated infliction of pain.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, after a granted table and provision, punishment also carries an echo of losing tasted sweetness and sustaining gift.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the concrete bridle branch of ح ك م beneath the adjective الحكيم. It remains anchored in the final paired names and is strengthened by the following assertion of complete capability. Downstream prose should mark it as a governing metaphor for self-disciplined power, not an etymological gloss or a limitation imposed from outside.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The adjacency of العزيز and الحكيم permits the force image of the first to meet the bridle image within the second root.

activation_trace.role: Overmastering force supplies the motion or power that requires no external aid.
The bridle that checks uncontrolled running images wisdom as power's internal governance.
Complete effective capacity confirms that the restraint is not inability.
Measured planning supplies the deliberative direction of the internally governed force.

changed_reading.before: Mighty and Wise are two independent honorifics.
changed_reading.after: As a contained metaphor, the ending images irresistible power carrying its own bridle: fully capable, yet never ungoverned.

strongest_changes: The conditionals become a witness-to-judge handoff rather than the speaker's private verdict.
The legal sequence makes punishment and pardon calibrated responses, while the shifted العزيز makes forgiveness an act of power.
The move from commanded worship to Your servants suggests that failed obedience does not cancel divine belonging.
Forgiveness gains a protective non-exposure mechanism, and the following truth verdict recasts restrained speech as truthful testimony.
summary.what_was_special: The pericope moves from proportioned consequence and guarded disclosure through formal testimony, received sign, limited witnessing, truthful speech, and universal dominion. That sequence turns a compact conditional into an unusually dense transfer of jurisdiction in which mercy remains powerful, knowing, and relational.
remaining_uncertainties: The belonging phrase may authorize punishment more strongly than it pleads against exclusion.
The non-exposure mechanism is a sequence-based inference rather than an explicit causal statement.
The deprivation and bridle readings are deliberately branch-distant material metaphors and should remain exploratory.
